reviewed_input: Complete definition and proof draft of CONNECTED_BAND_INTEGER_COMPENSATION.md; established frozen completion/modification supplied as premises. Source and final wording improvements are described below.
response:
ACCEPTThe new upper bound
$$|T|+|M|\le 18m+29\qquad(m\ge2)$$
is mathematically valid under the displayed hypotheses, including arbitrary actual rematching and retention of every old endpoint.I find no gap in the real-blank lemma, its strengthened left boundary, or the pocket coefficient identity. The open-board cover is correct with the stated zero contribution at its terminal boundary. The global color identity properly accommodates matching edges crossing between  $U$  and  $P_0$ .Sharpness is supported by the established completion and frozen modification that you explicitly supply as premises. The completion cardinalities alone would not establish feasibility or freezing, but your supplied modification theorem supplies those additional facts.This verdict concerns the written mathematics. It does not rely on the earlier fractional construction or the reported Python and Lean checks.1. The available-site enclosure is correctThe retained selections have row counts
$$3m+5,\quad 2m+3,\quad 1,\quad 2,\quad 3,\quad 0,$$
so
$$|R|=5m+14.$$
In particular, the retained row-four selections are exactly
$$(4,6),\qquad (4,6m+6),\qquad (4,6m+8).$$
The old matching consists of  $4(m+1)+1$  disjoint edges, giving
$$|P_0|=8m+10,\qquad |P_0\cap\mathrm{white}|=4m+5.$$
There is one subtlety in the forced-blank argument: not every retained selection is adjacent to an old endpoint. Specifically,
$$(0,3+6j),\qquad 0\le j\le m+1,$$
has no neighbor in  $P_0$ . The note does not assert otherwise, but this distinction matters when expanding “inspection of the displayed rows.”Every other retained selection is saturated by an old endpoint. Those saturated selections force all neighbors of the exceptional row-zero selections blank as well. Thus the exceptional selections do not introduce additional available sites.More explicitly, the sites outside  $R\cup P_0\cup U$  are exactly the following forced blanks:RowForced-blank columns $0$ All even columns  $0,2,\ldots,6m+8$  $1$  $\{0\}\cup\{3+6j:0\le j\le m+1\}$  $2$  $\{2,6m+9\}\cup\{4+6j,8+6j:0\le j\le m\}$  $3$  $\{0,2\}$  $4$  $\{1,5,7,6m+5,6m+7,6m+9\}$  $5$  $\{6,6m+6,6m+8\}$ Each entry is forced by a retained selection already adjacent to  $P_0$ . For example: $(4,6)$  forces  $(4,5),(4,7),(5,6)$  blank. $(4,6m+6)$  forces  $(4,6m+5),(4,6m+7),(5,6m+6)$  blank. $(4,6m+8)$  forces  $(4,6m+7),(4,6m+9),(5,6m+8)$  blank.Taking the complement of these sites together with  $R$  and  $P_0$  gives precisely the displayed  $C_m\sqcup A\sqcup I$ . No site of  $U$  is adjacent to  $R$ . Consequently,
$$T\setminus R\subseteq U,\qquad P\setminus P_0\subseteq U.$$
The component count is also correct:
$$|C_m|
=2m+3m+(6m-3)+(6m-1)
=17m-4.$$
These are coordinate facts valid for every  $m\ge2$ ; they do not require extrapolation from finite boards.2. The global matching color identity is exactBecause every grid edge has one white endpoint and  $M$  is an actual matching,
$$|M|=|P\cap\mathrm{white}|.$$
Also,  $T\setminus R$  and  $P\setminus P_0$  are disjoint and contained in  $U$ . Hence the definition of  $W$  gives
$$W(U)
=
|T\setminus R|
+
|(P\setminus P_0)\cap\mathrm{white}|.$$
Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
|T|+|M|
&=|R|+|T\setminus R|
  +|P_0\cap\mathrm{white}|
  +|(P\setminus P_0)\cap\mathrm{white}|\\
&=9m+19+W(U).
\end{aligned}$$
This argument counts endpoints of the single global matching. It does not require any old matching edge to survive, and it does not require a matching to close inside any individual piece of  $U$ .In particular, a crossing between  $U$  and  $P_0$  causes no discrepancy: its old endpoint remains in the fixed old-endpoint count, while its new endpoint is counted according to its color. Equation (2) is sound.3. The local real-blank lemma has no proof gapWrite
$$S=A+B+C+D+E+F+G,\qquad
s=x+y+z+u+v+w.$$
The stated case split is exhaustive, and every step works for real blanks in  $[0,1]$ .Case  $y=1$ Here  $A=B=E=1$ , and  $D\ge x$ .If  $z=1$ , then
$$C+F+G\ge3-B=2\ge z+w.$$
If  $z=0$ , the implication for  $w$ , together with nonnegativity, gives
$$C+F+G\ge w=z+w.$$
Thus
$$S\ge3+x+z+w\ge s,$$
because  $y=1$  and  $u+v\le2$ .Case  $y=0,\ z=1$ The group  $B+C+F+G$  contributes at least three.If either  $x=1$  or  $u=1$ , the disjoint group  $A+D+E$  contributes at least two. Consequently  $S\ge5$ , which covers all five potentially nonzero bits  $x,z,u,v,w$ .If  $x=u=0$ , then  $s=z+v+w\le3$ , so the first group already suffices.Case  $y=z=0,\ x=1$ Here  $A=D=1$ .If  $v=1$ , the disjoint group  $B+E+F$  contributes at least two, giving  $S\ge4$ , sufficient for  $x+u+v+w$ .If  $v=0$ , then
$$S\ge2+C+F\ge2+w\ge1+u+w=s.$$
Case  $x=y=z=0$ If  $u=v=1$ , adding their implications gives
$$A+B+D+2E+F\ge4.$$
Using  $E\le1$ ,
$$A+B+D+E+F\ge4-E\ge3,$$
which covers  $u+v+w$ .If exactly one of  $u,v$  is one, its condition supplies two units, sufficient for that bit and  $w$ . If neither is one, the condition for  $w$  suffices.Thus  $S\ge s$  is proved. No part of this reasoning assumes integral blanks. The binary nature of the six selection variables is used explicitly in the case split and in the bounds on their sums.The strengthened boundary form is an immediate corollaryThere is an even shorter proof of the strengthened statement than the one in the note.Suppose  $x=0$  and  $A=D=1$ . Replace  $x$  by  $x'=1$ , leaving every other variable unchanged. All six implications remain valid, since the only newly activated implication is precisely
$$x'=1\Longrightarrow A=D=1.$$
Applying the ordinary lemma gives
$$S\ge1+y+z+u+v+w=s+1.$$
So the extra boundary unit is fully justified. It is not an unsupported strengthening.4. The embedding and disjoint open-board cover are correct4.1 The local inequality gives the claimed weight boundFor even  $a$ , the six selection sites represented by  $x,y,z,u,v,w$  are black, and the seven sites represented by the blank variables are white. Consequently their formal colored weight is
$$s+(7-S).$$
The local lemma bounds this by seven.For  $a=6j$ ,  $2\le j\le m$ , the graph supplies all six implications:The old endpoints above  $x=(4,a)$  and  $y=(4,a+2)$  are  $(3,a)$  and  $(3,a+2)$ . Selecting  $x$  forces  $A=D=1$ ; selecting  $y$  forces  $A=B=E=1$ .The four neighbors of  $z$  are exactly the sites represented by  $B,C,F,G$ .The three neighbors of  $u$  are represented by  $A,D,E$ .The three neighbors of  $v$  are represented by  $B,E,F$ .For selected  $w$ , the two neighbors represented by  $C,F$  contain at most one occupied site, giving  $C+F\ge1$ .Ignoring the left neighbor of  $x$  and the right neighbor of  $w$  only relaxes necessary conditions. There is no periodic identification.4.2 The left boundary legitimately contributes sixAt  $a=6$ , the physical site  $(4,6)$  belongs to  $R$ , and its old endpoint neighbor  $(3,6)$  forces
$$o_{(4,7)}=o_{(5,6)}=0.$$
Thus  $A=D=1$ . The old endpoint  $(3,8)$  supplies the  $y$ -anchor.Using  $x=0$  for the selection increment, the strengthened inequality gives
$$s+(7-S)\le6.$$
The surviving terms are exactly the terms of  $W(L)$ , proving
$$W(L)\le6.$$
The phrase “three zero terms” is correct when read as three zero weight contributions:the selection increment at  $(4,6)$ ;the occupation at  $(4,7)$ ;the occupation at  $(5,6)$ .The blank variables  $A,D$  themselves equal one. This is a notation clarification, not a local proof gap.Equivalently, one can apply the ordinary lemma using the physical selection  $x=1$ , obtain a weight bound of seven, and subtract the retained selection’s unit.4.3 Both pair families have the required old-endpoint anchorsFor  $c=9+6i$ , the black site  $(3,c)$  has old endpoint neighbor  $(3,c-1)$ . Hence
$$o_{(2,c)}+t_{(3,c)}\le1.$$
For  $c=11+6i$ , the old endpoint neighbor is  $(3,c+1)$ , so the same inequality holds. At the final slot, this neighbor is
$$(3,6m+6)\in P_0,$$
which is still present. There is no terminal loss in the second pair family.4.4 The precise set identity includes one zero-weight terminal siteLet
$$B_a=\{(4,c),(5,c):a\le c\le a+5\}\cup\{(3,a+4)\},$$
and put
$$q=(4,6m+5).$$
Let  $P_i^-$  and  $P_i^+$  denote the two-site pairs at columns  $9+6i$  and  $11+6i$ , respectively. The exact disjoint set identity is
$$C_m\sqcup\{q\}
=
L
\sqcup
\bigsqcup_{i=0}^{m-1}(P_i^-\sqcup P_i^+)
\sqcup
\bigsqcup_{j=2}^{m}B_{6j}.$$
Its row-by-row verification is:SitesWhere they occurAll row-two sites of  $C_m$ The  $2m$  pairsRow-three columns  $9+6i,11+6i$ The same pairsRow-three column  $10$  $L$ Row-three columns  $16,22,\ldots,6m+4$ The distinct block extrasRow-four columns  $8,\ldots,11$  $L$ Row-four columns  $12,\ldots,6m+5$ The blocks, including  $q$ Row-five columns  $7,\ldots,11$  $L$ Row-five columns  $12,\ldots,6m+5$ The blocksThe terminal guard makes  $q$  a forced blank, so its occupation contribution is zero. One may either extend the weight by zero at  $q$ , as the text does, or delete  $q$  from the final block.This is the only set-level qualification needed. It is coordinate bookkeeping, not a failure of the local inequality or a missing boundary argument.For  $m=2$ , there is exactly one ordinary block,  $a=12$ , and the same identity applies. Therefore, for every allowed  $m$ ,
$$W(C_m)\le2m+6+7(m-1)=9m-1.$$
5. The pocket certificate and both upper-port mates check exactly5.1 The crossing list is exhaustiveThe only adjacency edges from  $A$  to  $P_0$  are
$$(2,5)--(1,5),\qquad
(2,5)--(2,6),\qquad
(3,5)--(3,6).$$
Other neighbors outside  $A$  are forced blank. Thus every matching edge meeting  $A$  is either internal or one of these crossings.Since  $U_0=(2,5)$  is white and  $V_0=(3,5)$  is black,
$$|P\cap A\cap\mathrm{white}|=e+x_U.$$
It follows that
$$W(A)=|T\cap A|+e+x_U.$$
Both possible upper-port edges are included in  $x_U$ ; the matching property prevents both from occurring simultaneously.5.2 All certificate inequalities are validFor a wedge
$$K_v+O_a+O_b\le2,$$
the case  $K_v=0$  follows from  $O_a,O_b\le1$ . The case  $K_v=1$  follows from the selected-degree restriction, since  $a,b$  are actual neighbors of  $v$ .The third row is also valid:
$$2K_{(3,3)}
+O_{(2,3)}+O_{(3,4)}+O_{(4,3)}
\le3.$$
If  $K_{(3,3)}=0$ , the three occupation terms total at most three. If  $K_{(3,3)}=1$ , they total at most one.For the fourth row, the old endpoint at  $(3,6)$  gives
$$K_{(3,5)}+O_{(2,5)}\le1.$$
Selecting  $(3,5)$  forces  $(2,5)$  blank.The weighted right-hand sum is indeed
$$1+4+3+4+2+2+8+6+2+6+1=39.$$
5.3 Site coefficients reproduce the claimed edge identityWrite the weighted left side as
$$\mathcal L
=\sum_{v\in A}\alpha_vO_v+\sum_{v\in A}\beta_vK_v.$$
Its complete coefficient table can be grouped as follows:Vertices  $v$  $\alpha_v$  $\beta_v$  $(2,3),(2,5),(3,4),(4,0),(4,3),(5,1),(5,5)$ 40 $(3,3),(3,5),(5,0)$ 04 $(4,2),(4,4),(5,3)$ 31 $(5,2),(5,4)$ 13Thus
$$\alpha_v+\beta_v=4$$
at every pocket vertex.Because selections and endpoints are disjoint and  $M$  is a matching,
$$O_v=K_v+\sum_{\substack{e\in M\\v\in e}}1.$$
This is an exact identity. Substitution gives coefficient four to every selection. An internal edge  $vw$  receives coefficient  $\alpha_v+\alpha_w$ .The pocket has seventeen internal grid edges: two horizontal edges in row three, two in row four, five in row five, and eight vertical edges. Their coefficients are:Internal-edge classNumberCoefficientThe four displayed  $H$ -edges47The two displayed  $E_0$ -edges25All remaining internal edges114In particular, the coefficient-seven edges are exactly
$$(3,4)--(4,4),\quad
(4,2)--(4,3),\quad
(4,3)--(4,4),\quad
(4,3)--(5,3),$$
and the coefficient-five edges are exactly
$$(5,1)--(5,2),\qquad
(5,4)--(5,5).$$
For a crossing, only its endpoint inside  $A$  contributes:CrossingCoefficient $(1,5)--(2,5)$ 4 $(2,5)--(2,6)$ 4 $(3,5)--(3,6)$ 0This explicitly handles both possible upper-port mates. The lower-port coefficient zero is also correct, because its endpoint inside  $A$  is black and contributes no endpoint term to  $W(A)$ .Consequently,
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L
&=4|T\cap A|+4e+4x_U+3H+E_0\\
&=4W(A)+3H+E_0.
\end{aligned}$$
There is no missing port term.Although  $K_{U_0}=0$  is forced by its two old endpoint neighbors, the expansion does not need to discard that variable: its selection coefficient is correctly four.5.4 The integer rounding is legitimateThe certificate yields
$$4W(A)+3H+E_0\le39.$$
Since  $H,E_0\ge0$  and  $W(A)$  is an integer,
$$W(A)\le\left\lfloor\frac{39}{4}\right\rfloor=9.$$
This establishes the pocket bound, including the upper-port-only case.6. The bounds combine to give the theoremBoth sites in  $I$  are black, so
$$W(I)\le2.$$
Their neighbors are in fact all forced blank, although the weight estimate needs only their colors and binary selection indicators.Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
W(U)
&=W(C_m)+W(A)+W(I)\\
&\le(9m-1)+9+2\\
&=9m+10.
\end{aligned}$$
The global identity now gives
$$J\le9m+19+9m+10=18m+29.$$
The board area is
$$6(6m+10)=36m+60,$$
so this is exactly
$$J\le\frac{\mathrm{area}}2-1.$$
Additional requirements to retain some permitted selections only restrict the feasible class, so the asserted upper bound for those subclasses follows immediately.7. Sharpness is supported under the supplied established constructionThe supplied completion sizes give
$$J(T^*,M_0)
=(13k+11)+(4k+1)
=17k+12.$$
Each specified modification removes two selections, adds one selection, and adds two matching edges. Thus
$$\Delta |T|=-1,\qquad \Delta |M|=2,\qquad \Delta J=1.$$
After all  $m$  modifications,
$$J=17(m+1)+12+m=18m+29.$$
Equivalently, the final sizes are
$$|T|=12m+24,\qquad |M|=6m+5.$$
Membership in the displayed permissions class also checks:The only removed old selections are  $g_i=(3,9+6i)$ .The other removed sites,  $(3,11+6i)$ , are not members of  $T_0$ , hence are not members of  $R$ .All  $h_i$  and  $f_i$  remain selected.The added matching endpoints lie outside  $P_0$ , and the endpoint sets of distinct slots are disjoint.The nontrivial remaining facts are that the completion contains the requisite auxiliary selections, that the modified configuration is feasible, and that it is completely frozen. Those facts do not follow merely from the two cardinalities or from disjointness of the slots. They follow from the established modification result expressly supplied in your question.Accordingly, the logical status is precise: the upper bound is proved within this note; the frozen equality example is obtained by applying the supplied earlier construction theorem. That is sufficient to support the exact maximum assertion here.For a version intended to stand entirely alone without that supplied result, the earlier theorem or explicit construction would need to be restated.8. The charge and token argument is validRows zero and one contain permanently
$$|T_{\mathrm{top}}|=5m+8,\qquad
|P_{\mathrm{top}}|=3m+4.$$
Their area is  $12m+20$ , so their total charge is
$$12m+20-2(5m+8)-(3m+4)=-m.$$
Here “unchanged” correctly means that the selected-site and endpoint sets in the top strip are unchanged. Its matching edges need not be unchanged under arbitrary rematching.The aligned  $2\times2$  tiles partition the board, and therefore
$$\sum_Qc(Q)
=\mathrm{area}-2|T|-|P|
=\mathrm{area}-2J
\ge2.$$
Subtracting the top-strip charge gives exterior charge at least  $m+2$ . By the definitions of  $C_{\mathrm{plus}}$  and  $C_{\mathrm{minus}}$ ,
$$C_{\mathrm{plus}}-C_{\mathrm{minus}}\ge m+2.$$
The ordered demand list has length  $C_{\mathrm{minus}}+m$ , whereas the positive token list has length  $C_{\mathrm{plus}}$ . An injection therefore exists, and the number of unused tokens is at least
$$C_{\mathrm{plus}}-(C_{\mathrm{minus}}+m)\ge2.$$
Since tokens are identified by  $(Q,j)$ , no physical positive half-unit is used twice. This proves exactly the stated aggregate compensation claim.The only wording refinements I recommend are to make the terminal zero-weight extension explicit in the set cover, identify the left-boundary “zero terms” as weight contributions, and name the precise earlier construction theorem used for frozen sharpness. None is a correction to the new upper-bound argument.
